shared_elements: carved grey stone surface in low relief
horizontal band or register line running across the surface
repeated vertical elongated motifs arranged in a row
fine parallel incised hatching/ribbing filling forms
justification: The most specific correspondence is a horizontal register line above a row of repeated, vertically oriented elongated motifs filled with fine parallel incisions — visible along the upper zone of the statue in A and forming the whole of the frieze in B, in similarly weathered grey stone worked in shallow relief. The biggest difference is scale and completeness of view: A is a whole three-dimensional figure whose surface carries varied, non-repeating elements (discs, curved bands, hook forms) scattered over a body, while B is a tight detail of a strictly serial, uniform ornamental band with no figural or circular motifs at all.
